title: Analytics & tags
summary: Analytics and tag managers on EDS are split across the loading phases instead of one monolithic container, and they wait for consent. Get this wrong and Lighthouse drops from 100 on the first tag.

items.title: Pick one stack
items.detail: Use the aem-martech plugin for Adobe Analytics, Web SDK and Tags, or aem-gtm-martech for Google Analytics and GTM.

items.title: Plugin, not one container
items.detail: Load Web SDK and the data layer from the plugin instead of a single Launch or GTM script in head.html.

items.title: No duplicate extensions
items.detail: Leave the Web SDK, Analytics and Target extensions out of the Tags property; the plugin adds them itself.

items.title: Data layer name matches
items.detail: Set dataLayerInstanceName to the same name as the ACDL extension in Launch (adobeDataLayer on both by default).

items.title: Tags load delayed
items.detail: Run the tag container in the delayed phase so its rules never compete with LCP.

items.title: Consent gates tracking
items.detail: Keep the plugin's default consent of pending and update it from your CMP; never grant consent by default.

items.title: Prerender aware
items.detail: Use the plugin's speculative prerender handling so prerendered pages do not count as page views.

items.title: Calls verified
items.detail: Confirm edge.adobedc.net interact and collect calls (or google-analytics.com collect) fire once consented.

items.title: Score still 100
items.detail: Run PageSpeed Insights on mobile with and without consent and keep the score at 100.

title: Target & personalization
summary: Adobe Target or Journey Optimizer personalizes EDS pages by fetching page modifications in the eager phase and applying them after blocks decorate. It costs LCP, so turn it on only where you personalize.

items.title: Try native first
items.detail: Check whether the built-in experimentation plugin covers the test before adding Target.

items.title: Web SDK path
items.detail: Integrate through the AEP Web SDK; keep at.js only for legacy setups.

items.title: Page-level flag
items.detail: Enable Target only on pages with metadata such as Target: on, not site-wide.

items.title: Datastream and org ID
items.detail: Configure the correct datastreamId and IMS orgId for each environment.

items.title: Apply after decoration
items.detail: Apply propositions once blocks report loaded, using a MutationObserver on block and section status.

items.title: Keep offers light
items.detail: Avoid heavy custom JavaScript in offers; it adds flicker and LCP on top of the baseline cost.

items.title: Consent before decisions
items.detail: Request personalization only when the visitor's consent allows it.

items.title: Interact call fires
items.detail: Confirm a call to edge.adobedc.net/ee/v1/interact on flagged pages and none on others.

items.title: LCP cost measured
items.detail: Compare LCP with and without the Target flag on mobile and desktop before rollout.

title: Experimentation
summary: The EDS experimentation plugin runs A/B tests, audiences and campaigns from page metadata, measured with operational telemetry. Authors set up a test in minutes; the checklist keeps it measurable and out of search.

items.title: Plugin installed
items.detail: Add the plugin under plugins/experimentation and call it from loadEager and loadLazy.

items.title: Experiment ID
items.detail: Give every test a unique ID such as OPT-0134 and reuse it across pages in the same test.

items.title: Challengers in a folder
items.detail: Put challenger pages in /experiments/<experiment-id>/ and publish them with the control.

items.title: Metadata rows
items.detail: Add Experiment and Experiment Variants to the control page metadata; set Experiment Split only to change the even split.

items.title: Variants not indexed
items.detail: Mark challengers noindex,nofollow via bulk metadata on /experiments/** or page metadata.

items.title: Audiences defined in code
items.detail: Define each audience as a function in experimentationConfig before authors reference it.

items.title: Preview the variants
items.detail: Check every variant on the .page preview with the simulation panel before publishing.

items.title: Enough traffic
items.detail: Raise RUM sampling on low-traffic test pages so results can reach significance.

items.title: Conversion defined
items.detail: Decide what counts as a conversion before launch; by default any click counts.

title: Operational telemetry
summary: Operational telemetry (RUM) is EDS's built-in, sampled, cookie-free field data: Core Web Vitals, errors, 404s and clicks per page view. It is how you prove a change worked in the field.

items.title: Sampling left on
items.detail: Keep the boilerplate's sampleRUM in aem.js; it collects about one in a hundred page views by default.

items.title: No personal data
items.detail: Never add personal data to custom checkpoints or source and target values.

items.title: Domain key access
items.detail: Get a domain key so the team can open the OpTel explorer for the production domain.

items.title: CWV green
items.detail: Check LCP, CLS and INP are green in the explorer; treat needs improvement as a problem.

items.title: Errors and 404s
items.detail: Review the error and 404 checkpoints after each release for new JavaScript errors and broken links.

items.title: Slow API calls
items.detail: Use the loadresource checkpoint to spot slow fragments and JSON endpoints.

items.title: Conversion defined
items.detail: Set a conversion definition in the explorer from the clicks that matter to the business.

items.title: Filter out bots
items.detail: Exclude bot traffic in the explorer before judging engagement or conversion numbers.

title: Consent management
summary: The EDS boilerplate gates all martech behind scripts/consent-check.js, which imports consented.js only after consent. Wiring a CMP such as OneTrust or Cookiebot into that gate keeps tracking legal and off the LCP path.

items.title: Replace the dummy
items.detail: Swap the boilerplate's decline-by-default consent-check.js for your real CMP wiring.

items.title: CMP loads delayed
items.detail: Inject the CMP script from consent-check.js, not head.html, to keep it off the critical path.

items.title: Martech in consented.js
items.detail: Put analytics, tag managers, personalization, pixels and chat widgets in consented.js only.

items.title: Essentials stay out
items.detail: Load login, cart and security code outside the consent gate; they are not martech.

items.title: Categories in tags
items.detail: Handle per-category consent in your tag manager or consented.js, not consent-check.js.

items.title: Banner timing agreed
items.detail: Agree with legal whether a banner that appears after load is acceptable before moving it earlier.

items.title: No layout shift
items.detail: Reserve space for the late banner or pin it to the bottom so it does not add CLS.

items.title: Nothing before consent
items.detail: Confirm consented.js and martech calls are absent until consent and consent.update fires both ways.

title: App Builder & APIs
summary: Most EDS integrations are blocks calling an API from the browser. Live traffic belongs on CDN edge workers, while App Builder suits author-side and background jobs. Choosing the right runtime keeps pages fast and secrets hidden.

items.title: Right runtime
items.detail: Call APIs from blocks for live traffic, use edge workers for middleware, and App Builder for author-side jobs.

items.title: No live App Builder
items.detail: Keep App Builder actions and AEM publish servlets out of the request path of live page views.

items.title: Secrets server-side
items.detail: Keep API keys in an edge worker or CDN header injection, never in block JavaScript.

items.title: Fetch after LCP
items.detail: Call APIs from blocks outside the first section so no second origin delays LCP.

items.title: Real pages via BYOM
items.detail: Render data-driven pages through a BYOM overlay or json2html so they are indexed and cached.

items.title: Actions secured
items.detail: Keep require-adobe-auth on App Builder actions that call Adobe APIs and add your own checks for third-party APIs.

items.title: Publish triggers polled
items.detail: Trigger downstream jobs on publish by polling the Audit Log API with an Admin API key.

items.title: API calls monitored
items.detail: Watch the loadresource checkpoint for slow or failing JSON endpoints after launch.
